perspective:
I, Maria Ortega, have access to the following from my own perspective:

- I work with Cheryl Benallie at a community center. We occasionally collaborate and have a growing personal friendship; we have discussed our different cultural backgrounds and personal experiences.
- At the community center, I saw Cheryl looking stressed and overwhelmed by stacks of paperwork and planning for a new community outreach project.
- I offered to help her. Cheryl said that would be amazing and that she could definitely use the help.
- I helped Cheryl with the project.
- Afterward, I observed Cheryl handling responsibilities better and seeming more confident.
- In a staff meeting, I suggested Cheryl lead the next phase of the project, saying she had shown aptitude and commitment.
- I heard the Team Leader say that was a good suggestion and ask Cheryl what she thought about taking on the role.
- I heard Cheryl thank me for my confidence in her and say she was ready to take on the challenge.
- I worried Cheryl might perceive my suggestion as overstepping, so I approached her privately.
- I told Cheryl I was glad and wanted to make sure she felt supported, not pressured.
- Cheryl told me she was a bit surprised but appreciated my support, and that my belief in her meant a lot.
- I felt relieved that Cheryl valued my honesty and support.
- I proposed that we co-lead the project together.
- Cheryl said that sounded fantastic, that my guidance had been invaluable, and that she thought we made a great team.
- Cheryl and I successfully collaborated on several projects, strengthening our partnership.
- I felt joyful about our synergy and asked Cheryl what she thought about teaming up for more future projects.
- Cheryl said she would love that, that working with me had been wonderful, and that she was excited about what we could achieve together.

I do not have access to any of Cheryl’s private thoughts or feelings except what she directly told me or what I observed in her behavior.
